name: iam:PassRole + ssm:CreateDocument + ssm:StartAutomationExecution
description: Create a custom SSM Automation document with a Python aws:executeScript step, then start an execution that passes a privileged IAM role as AutomationAssumeRole. SSM runs the embedded Python in AWS-managed serverless compute under the admin role's credentials — no EC2 instance, Lambda function, or container is required. The selected payload determines what IAM action to perform.
author: Seth Art

required.description: Must be able to pass the target admin IAM role to the SSM Automation service as AutomationAssumeRole

additional.description: Poll execution status to confirm the Python script ran successfully

admin: A role must exist that trusts ssm.amazonaws.com to assume it
The role must have the permissions needed by the selected payload (e.g., iam:AttachUserPolicy for backdoor/attach-policy)
lateral: A role must exist that trusts ssm.amazonaws.com and has elevated permissions

references.title: Using scripts in runbooks (aws:executeScript) - AWS Systems Manager
Setting up Automation - AWS Systems Manager

options.name: ROLE_ARN
options.description: ARN of the IAM role to pass as AutomationAssumeRole (must trust ssm.amazonaws.com and have the permissions needed by the selected payload)

options.name: PAYLOAD
options.description: Payload to execute via SSM Automation Python step (run 'payloads list' to see available options)

options.name: DOCUMENT_NAME
options.description: Name for the SSM Automation document to create

options.name: REGION
options.description: AWS region for SSM Automation execution

options.name: CLEANUP
options.description: Delete the SSM Automation document after execution. Note: the starting user typically lacks ssm:DeleteDocument — use 'workspace cleanup' with admin credentials instead.
